ranked_routes.target_residue: C194 (linker, EIPYQ-C-PMTFG; pKa not reported but ABPP-ligandable in 4 chemoproteomic datasets)
ranked_routes.mechanism: Covalent warhead on the uniquely-positioned linker cysteine C194 fused to an E3-ligase handle (preferably VHL/RNF rather than CRBN) to drive proximity-induced ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of full-length IRF4. Function-block is NOT required — a 'silent' site is ideal for a degrader, since you only need durable, selective engagement to recruit the ligase.
ranked_routes.feasibility: Most de-risked of the differentiated routes. C194 is the ONLY literature-validated ligandable IRF4 cysteine (Resnick/Backus scout-fragment, ACS Cent Sci 2021) and recurs in chemoproteomic data. Degradation precedent for the target exists (dIRF4-2, the first IRF4 PROTAC, Nat Chem Biol 2026) and the clinical benchmark (ION251/frenlosirsen ASO) validates that lowering IRF4 levels is therapeutic in MM. A covalent anchor is conceptually straightforward to test.
ranked_routes.selectivity: IRF4-UNIQUE. The disordered linker (135-237) is the least-conserved region of the family; EIPYQ-C-PMTFG (and even the short PYQC) is absent from IRF8, IRF1, IRF3. This is the strongest true paralog-selectivity handle, and it is a covalent handle the one existing PROTAC (dIRF4-2) does NOT use — dIRF4-2 binds a CONSERVED IAD/PU.1 surface and rescues selectivity only via the degradation step + proteomics. A covalent-C194 + non-CRBN-ligase PROTAC is genuine white space.
ranked_routes.rationale: Best risk-adjusted play: pairs the single most ligandability-validated, paralog-selective cysteine with a modality (degradation) that tolerates a functionally silent site and is already clinically validated for IRF4 level-lowering. CRBN space is crowded and carries IKZF1/3 neosubstrate baggage, so a covalent C194 anchor on VHL/RNF differentiates on both target selectivity (the unique Cys) and E3 choice.

ranked_routes.route: Autoinhibition / dimer-interface trap at C250 (reframed as a covalent monomer-locking wedge)
ranked_routes.target_residue: C250 (IAD N-edge, LAFSD-C-RLHIC; pKa 7.1, ligandable thiolate; adjacent C255 must be disambiguated)
ranked_routes.mechanism: REFRAMED from the founder's original 'restore an IRF3-type closed latch.' The defensible mechanism is a covalent wedge at the IAD N-edge that locks IRF4 in a transcriptionally incompetent monomeric state by blocking the productive homodimer or the PU.1/BATF (EICE/AICE) partner interface — NOT by re-folding an IRF3-style buried hydrophobic core.
ranked_routes.feasibility: Highest novelty but least experimentally de-risked. C250 sits at the ordered IAD N-edge (~238 onward), pKa 7.1 is consistent with surface ligandability, and no disclosed program targets a covalent conformational/interface lock here. BUT the original 'IRF3 closed-latch' framing is contradicted by 5BVI/SAXS: IRF4's C-terminal autoinhibitory region (~420-450) is intrinsically flexible and does NOT fold into the IAD bundle, and C250 is at the OPPOSITE (N-terminal) end of the domain from that tail. The interface-wedge mechanism is plausible but unproven and must be shown experimentally.
ranked_routes.selectivity: IRF4-UNIQUE at the residue level. LAFSD-C-RLHIC has no Cys-bearing counterpart in IRF8 (aligned stretch HHSAFSQMVISFYY), IRF1, or IRF3. Strong paralog-selectivity handle, second only to C194.
ranked_routes.rationale: Highest-novelty, fully-white-space mechanism with a genuinely IRF4-selective cysteine — every other IAD effort targets the PU.1 face non-covalently. Ranked second (not first) only because the mechanism is the founder's hypothesis rather than a structurally demonstrated fact, so it carries the most discovery risk. If the wet experiments confirm an interface-disrupting adduct, this becomes the most differentiated program.

ranked_routes.target_residue: C99 (DBD recognition helix alpha3, KTRLR-C-ALNK; pKa 5.3 hyperreactive thiolate, ABPP-ligandable) primary; K94 (DPPTW-K-TRLR, phosphate-proximal basic residue) secondary Lys-directed option
ranked_routes.mechanism: Covalent adduct on C99 Sgamma directly destroys the recognition H-bond to adenine N6 (7JM4) and adds steric bulk inside the major groove, abolishing ISRE/EICE/GAAA engagement; kinact/KI capture during the apo/unbound dwell, NOT Kd competition — once alkylated, that IRF4 cannot re-engage DNA regardless of DNA's nM affinity. K94 warhead (sulfonyl fluoride/SuTEx) neutralizes a backbone-anchoring positive charge.
ranked_routes.feasibility: Mechanistically the most structurally grounded (7JM4 anchor; C99 is a buried, conserved, base-contacting recognition-helix thiol; R98/C99 genetically required for GAAA recognition) and backed by the cleanest covalent-TF-DBD precedent (DrugMap NF-kB1 ligand blocks DNA binding; STAT3 C468). The pKa 5.3 hyperreactive thiolate is exactly the kinetic situation where covalent capture beats DNA competition. Open question: C99 is buried/shielded in the DNA-BOUND state, so labeling depends on apo-state exposure/reactivity in a FOLDED, DNA-competent construct, not just lysate ABPP.
ranked_routes.selectivity: WORST. C99 is CONSERVED across the family (IRF4/IRF8 share TWKTRLR-C-ALNK verbatim; IRF8 C84; IRF1 has aligned Cys; only IRF3 has Ser) — a pan-IRF liability, not an IRF4 handle. K94 is likewise pan-family conserved. Only hope is kinetic (pKa 5.3) rather than sequence selectivity, which is weak. Most-competed route too (non-covalent DBD inhibitors G1126/SH514, plus ION251 and the (S)-H1 IAD binder).
ranked_routes.rationale: Ranked last despite being the most structurally compelling and precedented mechanism, because it inherits BOTH the conservation liability (would hit IRF8/IRF1) and the crowded competitive field. A C99 warhead is the best scientific demonstration of covalent IRF4 inhibition but the weakest commercial/selectivity position; reserve it as a chemical-probe/proof-of-mechanism arm rather than the lead therapeutic program.

modeling_plan: PRIMARY TEMPLATE IS IRF4'S OWN STRUCTURE, NOT IRF3. The IRF3 templates set the two conformational endpoints but cannot model the C250 region directly because IADs are in the twilight zone (own Needleman-Wunsch: IRF4 vs IRF3 ~30%, vs IRF5 ~26%). Plan: (1) Build the IRF4 IAD from PDB 5BVI (mouse IRF4 IAD-DeltaC, residues 238-420) as the primary template — first align human Q15306 to the 5BVI mouse construct to confirm co-numbering, since mouse/human IRF4 are ~94% identical through the IAD and C250/C255/C274 map directly; or start from AlphaFold2/AF3 full-length human IRF4 (well-supported given 5BVI + DBD structures 2DLL/6TD4/7O56/7OOT) and validate against 5BVI plus the NAR 2021 IRF4/DNA homodimer (Escalante, PubMed 33533913). (2) Use the IRF3 templates ONLY to define the two endpoint geometries the C250 adduct might bias between: 1QWT and 1J2F as the CLOSED/autoinhibited reference, and 3A77 (phospho-Ser386 IRF3) plus the IRF5 pseudophospho dimer 3DSH as the ACTIVE/DIMER-interface reference (the C-terminal AI segment becoming an extended dimer strand). Restrict cross-IRF homology use to the conserved beta-barrel core; do NOT trust it for the divergent AR/latch. (3) Map C250 AND C255 onto 5BVI and the IRF4 homodimer; compute solvent accessibility (SASA) and whether each side chain points into the dimer/PU.1(EICE)/BATF(AICE) interface vs into solvent — this is the decisive structural test of the wedge hypothesis. (4) Covalently dock the warhead in silico, then run MD/FEP (or MM-GBSA) comparing apo vs C250-adducted IRF4 on the stability (dG) of (a) the modeled inactive/monomeric state and (b) the productive homodimer and IRF4-PU.1-DNA EICE complex; the program-supporting prediction is that the adduct destabilizes the dimer/partner interface MORE than the monomer, shifting equilibrium toward inactive monomer. (5) Explicitly check whether the modeled adduct sterically/electrostatically clashes with the active dimer interface built from 3DSH/3A77 geometry. NOTE the framing correction: model C250 as an interface/dimerization wedge, NOT as a restorer of an IRF3-type buried closed latch — 5BVI/SAXS show IRF4's AR is flexible and unfolded and C250 is at the IAD N-edge, distal to the C-terminal tail that does IRF3-style switching.
first_experiments: 1. Intact-protein + peptide-level site-of-labeling and selectivity on FOLDED, FULL-LENGTH IRF4. Treat recombinant full-length (or DBD+IAD) IRF4 with the candidate warhead(s) and use intact-MS and LC-MS/MS to (a) confirm the adduct is on the intended cysteine and (b) disambiguate C250 vs adjacent C255 vs the silent C194 vs the other 12 Cys. Run head-to-head counter-screens against recombinant IRF8 (and IRF1) to test paralog selectivity at the conserved positions (C99/IRF8-C84, C274/IRF8-C226) — since only kinetic pKa, not sequence, protects those sites. This single experiment gates ALL three routes.

2. Apo-DBD covalent labeling coupled to EMSA/gel-shift for the C99 DNA-block thesis. Show, in a folded DNA-binding-competent IRF4 DBD construct, that a C99 adduct forms in the apo state (intact-MS) AND abolishes ISRE/EICE GAAA binding by EMSA/fluorescence-anisotropy. This is the decisive test of whether labeling kinetics (kinact/KI at the pKa-5.3 thiol) outrun the DNA on-rate and whether C99 is accessible when not DNA-bound (it is buried/shielded in the holo state). Measure kinact/KI to quantify the kinetic-vs-competition argument.

3. Functional consequence of C250 engagement for the autoinhibition/wedge hypothesis. After confirming C250 labeling (Exp 1), test whether the adduct (a) destabilizes the productive homodimer / PU.1(EICE) and BATF(AICE) partner complexes by EMSA/reporter assays and co-IP, and (b) shifts IRF4 toward monomer (SEC-MALS / native MS / thermal shift on apo vs adducted IAD). For the C194 degrader route, the parallel decisive test is a ternary-complex/degradation readout (cellular IRF4 knockdown by a C194-warhead-E3 conjugate), since C194 is functionally silent and only works via proximity, not function-block.
bottom_line: Yes — IRF4 is now a credible covalent target, but the credible play is NOT the obvious one. The route ranking inverts the founder's likely instinct: the DNA-interface block at C99, although the most structurally grounded (buried base-contacting recognition-helix thiol in 7JM4, pKa 5.3, real covalent-TF-DBD precedent from DrugMap NF-kB1 and STAT3 C468), is the WORST commercial bet because C99 is conserved across IRF4/IRF8/IRF1 (a pan-IRF liability) and the DBD field is crowded. The two differentiated, near-white-space routes both ride IRF4-UNIQUE cysteines in the least-conserved regions: a covalent degrader anchored on the validated, paralog-selective linker C194 (best risk-adjusted — degradation tolerates a silent site, is clinically de-risked by ION251, and a covalent + non-CRBN-E3 conjugate is white space), and an autoinhibition/dimer-interface wedge at the unique IAD-edge C250 (highest novelty, fully white space). The honest caveat: C250's mechanism is still a hypothesis, NOT a fact — the founder's 'IRF3-type closed-latch' framing is contradicted by 5BVI/SAXS (IRF4's autoinhibitory tail is flexible and unfolded, and C250 sits at the opposite N-terminal end of the IAD), so it must be re-pitched and proven as an interface/dimerization wedge. And the universal gating uncertainty across all three routes is the same: whether these cysteines (C99, C250, C194) are actually solvent-accessible and covalently ligandable in FOLDED, full-length IRF4 with retained fold and the predicted functional consequence — not just in denatured lysate ABPP digests. Resolve that with the intact-protein labeling + paralog counter-screen first; everything else follows.
